text:
emily chen: hey all, newbie stumbling over local DB networking. I did `docker compose up` and app logs show `could not translate host name \"postgres\"` then falls back to 127.0.0.1 and fails. I'm on Intel mac, Docker Desktop latest.

emily chen: compose (trimmed):
```yaml
services:
  web:
    build: .
    environment:
      - DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pw@postgres:5432/app_dev
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    volumes:
      - ./pg:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```

emily chen: I swear I didn't change hostnames, not sure why name isn't resolving inside container. :confused:

roberto diaz: welcome emily! quick sanity: are you running `docker compose up web` (a single service) or `docker compose up`? If you only start web, other services might not start unless `depends_on` present. Also check profiles.

emily chen: good call, I did `docker compose up web` because I wanted to iterate fast. I thought depends_on would be implicit.

roberto diaz: depends_on must be declared. Add `depends_on: - postgres` to web or start both. Also `docker compose ps` will show running services.

emily chen: added depends_on and re-ran; now postgres container appears but web still logs trying 127.0.0.1.

kevin li: two more checks: 1) Are you building the web binary on host and mounting into container? That can cause stale config. 2) Print env inside web container: `docker compose exec web env | grep DATABASE_URL`.

emily chen: I ran the env check and the container has the correct DATABASE_URL pointing at postgres. `ping postgres` from web container works. But the app binary still tries socket/localhost.

roberto diaz: many frameworks have layered config. Maybe your app reads a runtime config file or falls back to `.env.local`. Try `docker compose exec web sh -c 'printenv DATABASE_URL; ls -la /app && cat /app/config/local.yml 2>/dev/null'` to see what's being used.

emily chen: ahhh the repo has a `./config/local.yml` that's mounted into container and it had `database: host: 127.0.0.1`. I missed that. Removing the host entry or setting it to `postgres` fixes it.

kevin li: nice catch. Also if you want to run web on host while still using container postgres, set `DATABASE_URL` on host to `postgresql://postgres:pw@localhost:5432/app_dev` and ensure `ports` mapping is present and not blocked by host postgres. Or just run the web in-container for parity.

emily chen: fixed by updating mount and removing old local.yml. Postgres reachable, migrations ran. Thanks so much! I'll add a note to onboarding about docker vs host runs and the local config file. :sparkles:

devx-bot: Tip: onboarding doc updated with a checklist: 1) prefer `docker compose up` for first-run, 2) use `depends_on` for dev services, 3) avoid mounting host config that overrides env. See https://redwood.internal/devenv/onboarding for examples.
